summary.headline: The Elementary School Building Committee eliminated Option 4 for Neary School and voted to focus design efforts on Options 1, 3, and a $15M baseline.
summary.summary: Architects from Tappe Architects presented updated schematic massings, site reconfigurations, and a preliminary cost model ranging from roughly $24 million to nearly $50 million for Neary Elementary School renovations and additions. Educators and school administrators voiced strong consensus favoring Option 3, which encloses the central courtyard for a full-sized gymnasium and keeps the school footprint intact. The committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 due to high costs and site disruption, and voted unanimously to direct the consultants to focus future work on Option 1, Option 3, and an alternative aligning with Town Meeting's $15 million scope placeholder.

topics.title: Stakeholder meetings and site plan reconfiguration
topics.summary: Tappe Architects reviewed recent meetings with first responders, the DPW, and Neary educators. The designers proposed an updated site circulation layout to improve drop-off queuing and stormwater issues by routing passenger car drop-off around the back near the cafeteria while keeping buses at the front canopy. Neary teachers and staff expressed a clear preference for Option 3 over other layouts.
key_details: First responder and DPW meeting occurred September 9, 2026, covering security, access, and snow removal.
Educator and administrator meeting on September 16, 2026, yielded strong staff consensus for Option 3.
Proposed site plan routes buses to the front entrance and loops parent vehicles around the rear cafeteria entrance to prevent backups on the access road.
Option 4 would push site circulation into existing play fields, creating site logistical issues.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; site plan concepts will be refined.

topics.title: Educational heat map and architectural options
topics.summary: The district presented an updated educational heat map evaluating how Options 1, 2, 2.1, 3, and 4 meet educational program goals. Options 3 and 4 satisfy all criteria, while Option 2 presents tradeoffs, including a undersized gymnasium and lack of dedicated teacher collaboration spaces. Option 3 fills the existing interior courtyard to create a full gymnasium and keeps recreational fields and play spaces intact.
key_details: Option 2 is an interior renovation with a smaller elementary gym.
Option 2.1 evaluates adding a larger 1,700-square-foot front entry and administrative vestibule.
Option 3 infills the interior courtyard for a full-sized gym and bleachers, leaving existing fields intact.
Option 4/4.1 builds a new exterior gym wing, requiring significant site regrading and displacing play fields.
topics.outcome: Committee received the updated heat map evaluation.

topics.title: Preliminary cost analysis and option elimination
topics.summary: Consultants presented comparative preliminary cost estimates for each option, incorporating an estimated $4.5 million roof replacement. Total project costs were estimated between $24.4 million and $49.2 million depending on the option, prompting committee discussion on how to reconcile proposals with the $15 million figure previously cited at Town Meeting. The committee voted to officially eliminate Option 4 and instructed consultants to focus on Options 1, 3, and a scoped $15 million baseline.
key_details: Option 1 base code renovation estimated at $24.4M construction cost, $29.8M to $34.6M total project cost.
Option 2 estimated at $34.5M total project cost; Option 2.1 estimated at $38.3M total project cost.
Option 3 estimated at $38.5M total project cost with roof ($31.6M without roof).
Option 4.1 estimated at $49.2M total project cost with roof ($44.7M without roof).
A true $15 million budget would only address urgent code, accessibility, and partial HVAC/roof repairs without educational improvements.
topics.outcome: Option 4 was eliminated by a 3-1 vote. Consultants were directed to focus on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million scope option by a 4-0 vote.
topics.why_it_matters: The town faces project costs ranging from $15 million for basic system repairs up to nearly $40 million for comprehensive school modernization, directly affecting municipal borrowing and taxpayers.

topics.title: Next steps and meeting schedule
topics.summary: The committee established upcoming milestones leading to the October 17 Town Meeting. The next committee meeting was scheduled for October 15, 2026, to review refined presentation materials and finalize recommendations.
key_details: Consultants will deliver presentation drafts by October 13, 2026.
Next Elementary School Building Committee meeting scheduled for October 15, 2026.
Outreach planned with the Select Board, School Committee, and Recreation Commission.
Presentation to Town Meeting scheduled for October 17, 2026.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The chair called for public comment, and seeing no hands raised, entertained a motion to adjourn the meeting.
key_details: No members of the public requested to speak during the open public comment period.
The meeting adjourned at approximately 8:20 PM.

votes.motion: Direct consultants to focus their work on Option 1, Option 3, and an analysis of a $15 million scope option

public_comment.summary: The Recreation Commission chair asked the committee to engage the Recreation Commission and youth sports organizations before eliminating options or finalizing site changes, noting concerns about impacts to parking, athletic fields, and indoor gym availability on weekends.
